From Caves to Cubes: A History of Mapping

The Early Days

Before the term video mapping existed, humans were already mapping the world through light and surface.

In the depths of the Grotte de Lascaux, Chauvet and Pech Merle in France, the first image-makers discovered that the irregular shapes of the cave walls could become part of the image itself.

The convex curves of rock became the flanks of a bison, the shadow of a torch made an animal appear to move.

These early artists weren't just painting; they were mapping — using the architecture of the world as a canvas, embedding illusion within matter.

The rock surface was not neutral background but a collaborator, a primitive topology for representation.

 

The renaissance

Centuries later, this same dialogue between image and space found new expression in the Renaissance.

The discovery of linear perspective by Brunelleschi and Alberti was, in essence, a mathematical form of mapping — a way to project three-dimensional reality onto a two-dimensional plane.

Artists like Pere Borrell del Caso, with his 1874 painting Escaping Criticism, pushed the illusion to its paradoxical limit: the figure literally steps out of the frame. The painted world invades the viewer’s world.

The image reclaims space. This is the spirit of trompe-l’œil — a trick of the eye that anticipates every future experiment where image and reality blur.

 

 

By the Baroque era, illusion expanded beyond the canvas to encompass whole architectures. The frescoes of Andrea Pozzo at Sant’Ignazio in Rome transformed ceilings into infinite heavens, merging painting, perspective, and built space.

Churches became immersive environments — proto-domes of projection — where light and geometry conspired to suspend disbelief.

The human eye was now inside the image.

 

The Projector

With the twentieth century came the dematerialization of image and matter.

The paintbrush gave way to the projector. French architect and artist Hans Walter Müller, beginning in the 1960s, developed inflatable architectures and projected diapositives onto their translucent membranes, sometimes inside natural caves, calling these "topoprojections".

His environments breathed, expanded, and glowed — living architectures of light. Müller’s work fused the ephemeral and the structural, prefiguring the “mapped” light architectures that would come decades later.

 

 

In the 1980s, American artist Michael Naimark introduced a crucial shift: the feedback loop between real space and projected image.

In his project Displacements (1980–84), he filmed a domestic scene using a rotating camera, then projected the same footage back into the same space using a rotating projector. The result was uncanny — a ghost of the recorded world haunting its original location.

Time, memory, and perspective were mapped together. Here the image no longer represents space; it inhabits it.

Naimark’s moving projection becomes a spatial event — a living cartography of perception.

 

 

Parallel explorations emerged in experimental cinema and performance art: Krzysztof Wodiczko projected faces of marginalized voices onto urban monuments, politicizing architecture through illumination.

His works redefined the relationship between body, space, and image — each was a step toward mapping as a live, spatial, and social practice.

 

The Digital Age

By the 2000s, this lineage converged in the rise of video mapping, as digital technology enabled real-time alignment of image and architecture.

The artist collective EXYZT, later evolving into 1024 Architecture, translated this long history of illusion into the language of pixels, code, and stage performance.

In Étienne de Crécy’s “Beats and Cubes” live shows (2007), they constructed a luminous cubic structure whose geometry was mapped with video and synchronized with electronic sound. The cube pulsed, folded, and unfolded in sync with the beat — architecture became instrument, façade became choreography.

The legacy of Lascaux’s shadows returned, now algorithmically controlled, projected on modular space instead of stone.

 

 

From 2010 onward, the story of mapping entered a new chapter with the creation of MadMapper, a software developed by artists, for artists.

Conceived by the Geneva-based studio GarageCube (creators of Modul8) in collaboration with 1024 Architecture, MadMapper distilled the complex craft of projection alignment into an intuitive visual interface.

What had once required specialized engineering became a fluid act of creation — drawing with light in real space.

This tool opened the field to a generation of designers, musicians, VJs, and visual artists, transforming mapping from an experimental niche into a widespread artistic language.

Like the pigments of Lascaux or the perspective grids of the Renaissance, MadMapper became the new brush of its era — a technology that democratized illusion, empowering anyone to sculpt space with light.

A Software for Artists

From 2010 onward, the story of mapping entered a new chapter with the creation of MadMapper, a software developed by artists, for artists. Conceived by GarageCube in collaboration with 1024 Architecture, MadMapper distilled the complex craft of projection alignment into an intuitive visual interface. What had once required specialized engineering became a fluid act of creation — drawing with light in real space. This tool opened the field to a generation of designers, musicians, VJs, and visual artists, transforming mapping from an experimental niche into a widespread artistic language. Like the pigments of Lascaux or the perspective grids of the Renaissance, MadMapper became the new brush of its era — a technology that democratized illusion, empowering anyone to sculpt space with light.

 

 

Today, mapping is no longer an illusion of depth on a surface — it is a method of composing reality itself.

From painted caves to digital architectures, each epoch redefined the link between image and world, light and structure.

The gesture remains the same: to reveal the hidden space between matter and vision, between seeing and being seen.

As the beam of a projector finds its surface, we are still in the cave, tracing the contours of the world with light.

MadMapper Recent Highlights

Meet MadMapper 6

 

Geneva, TBA, 2025

 

MadMapper 6 is now available for purchase on madmapper.com. 

Users who pre-ordered the v6 upgrade can now download it directly from the Downloads section of their Account page.

 

This major upgrade introduces powerful new tools that let creators explore mapping ideas more freely, perform more intuitively in live settings, and synchronize entire shows with the brand-new Timeline feature. It’s been one of our community’s most requested additions, and we’re thrilled to finally bring it to the MAD universe.

 

MadMapper’s interface has also received a refined visual overhaul. While everything remains where you expect it, the experience is cleaner and sharper. For a quick tour of what’s new, check out the “MadMapper 6 at a Glance” page.

 

To support users worldwide, we’re also launching this new MAD Documentation platform, offering a more accessible learning experience than ever. Alongside it, the MAD Certified program is now live on our website, making it easy to find and connect with certified artists, schools, and training partners around the globe.

 

Welcome to the new era of MadMapper!

 

The MAD team

v6 New features

Timelines

A long awaited feature, the timelines now allow for any parameter animation. Sculpt your animation curves in realtime, pick your keyframe interpolation method, from Bezier to Flat interpolation, we've got you covered. Add audio, sync to the music et voila!

Montage Tracks

Compose your story, experiment. Create as many montage tracks as you like as with non linear editing software. Cut, chop, arrange or time-reverse your medias the easy way.  Before or once you’ve crafted your montage track, simply assign it to the surface of your choice. MadMapper will take care of the details!

Timelines Grid

Upgrade your good ol' Scenes and Cues grid to animation. Improvise, combine, surprise yourself. Multiple timelines offer the flexibility to improvise by managing various sequences and switching between them to respond to the moment. Additionally, you can define even a trigger exclusivity.

The Conductor

It's the Conduct of your entire show ! Its dedicated view lets you organize your entire project, providing the info your need at your fingertips, and features a bird's eye view of your entire show. You can also use it to montage timelines !

Animation Clips

MadMapper 6 also introduces Clips : short, repeatable, and loopable segments. These are ghostable and can be consolidated as unique elements as well. It's a great way to manipulate your content !

Audio Tracks

Audio tracks come with advanced FFT analysis and automated BeatTracking to snapping points, offering powerful new options for audiovisual synchronization. It provides a visually stunning and practical way to see audio frequencies, making it easier than ever to snap triggers with precision. on the beat. A wonder for syncing visual elements to the music !

Time Markers

Within your timeline tracks, you can set up markers with follow actions to bring basic logic and interactivity to your timelines. Wait for specific events such as button presses, custom goto to jump to specific parts of your show based on different actions and so on... Booya !

Export to File

Another game-changer: you can now bake your entire mapping, including Laser, DMX, Video, and Audio elements, all in one go!  Whether it’s your entire project or just a loop section, simply click the Export button in the top-right corner of the timeline and you'll get access to this export window including audio, video codecs settings, and more.

DMX samplers

DMX fixtures now sample directly into the output composition! Composite surfaces in realtime and convert your layer stack to light ! By default, this enables automatic DMX canvas generation, but for more accuracy you can also define a custom DMX canvas for pixel-perfect control. Plus you can create multiple canvas instances in the projectors tab.

New UI

We've worked hard on a UI refresh to give your favorite software a more professional look and feel. One more standout change: the media pool is now conveniently positioned on the left, right beside the surfaces in order to put everything you need within easy reach. One trick though - if you prefer the previous layout, you can switch back via the View / Separate Media Tab menu (or the icon top right of the interface). However keeping media on the left greatly improves comfort and workflow when using the timeline !

Offline Library

No more reliance on online materials and fx ! When you first start MadMapper, your entire library downloads directly to your computer, making it so much more convenient for offline work. The Library tab therefore hosts all your materials and fx, giving you quick access whether you're online or offline !

Projects workspace & Consolidation

We’ve significantly enhanced project structure capabilities, now embedded in a local workspace. So you create a project, save it, and instead of having a .mad project, you now get a local workspace hosting your entire project. The workspace includes everything ! From materials and media to auto-saves, making it easier than ever to keep all project elements in one clean, accessible location. Collect and save your ressources from the File menu, then simply copy this entire folder to transfer your project to another computer !

Release Notes v6.0.0

ADDITIONS

 

+ Added Timelines:
    + Timelines are replacing Cues, they are like Cues but all parameters can be animated
    + Visuals can be added in Montage Tracks and used as visual for video / laser layers
    + Audio Track
    + OSC / MIDI Output tracks
    + Markers allow interactivity on timeline playback
    + Conductor is the master timeline, it can be synced to an external Time Code (MIDI MTC / Audio LTC / ArtNet TimeCode)
    + Montage tracks control media playback (Movies, Materials, Generators etc.)
    + Surface FX Timebase can be controlled by timelines playyback
    + Export your timeline to get movies for each Video Output, ILDA file for each Laser Output, Audio File for all audio in timeline (audio tracks & montage tracks), MadLight Sequence for DMX Output
    + Timeline in grid (not conductor) can be synched to BPM with Quantized Launch & BPM Sync Playback. Sync your Video, your LEDs, Lights & Lasers with Ableton Link
+ MadMapper Projects are now stored in a folder with resources (workspace)
    + Menu File / Collect and Save allows you to import all necessary resources (Materials, movies, audio files etc.) so your project can be easiely moved to another computer
+ MadLight:
    + DMX Fixtures are now in the output and sampling video surfaces
+ User Interface
    + Major refresh
    + Support more display scale ratio on Windows (like scaling 150%, before MadMapper supported 100% or 200% but not inbetween)
    + Media Tab is on left side by default, can be extracted on the right side with menu View / Extract Media Tab or with toolbar button
    + Surface Lines & Masks list can be resized
    + Added a "Show Surfaces Names" option in Input View and Output Preview Settings
    + Added a "Switch to media" button in surface inspector
    + Added keyboard shortcuts for object-tabs (media, video surfaces, laser surfaces, etc)
+ Project management
    + Added a project export function
+ MadLaser:
    + Added Laser Circle surface type
    + Implemented laser mask feathering (on Laser Quad & Laser Output)
    + Added distortion transform on Laser Output (fixes projector pincushion distortion)
    + Added laser Generator "Laser FX" to apply a Laser Line FX to a vector source visual
+ Audio
    + Added Audio Equalizer in Master tab (4 bands, high quality)
    + Added Audio Routing on movies & timeline audio tracks (multi channel input / multi channel output => routing matrix available)
+ MIDI / OSC outputs can be defined in Project Settings
+ Support render passes in ISFs
+ Library resources (Materials etc.) are available offline (when no internet)
+ Added Svg Image player (add image / choose an SVG file) => you can get a vector input with colors for lasers surfaces and a adjustable size SVG for video surfaces
+ Added a way to re-enable discarded audio devices in Preferences
+ Added option to replace a Material / Generator etc. with another on a visual in Media Bin (right click / Replace ...)
+ Added Windows Audio Session as audio driver type option in preferences (WASAPI)
+ Added an synchronised Favorites collection in Library
+ Added a way to re-enable discarded video-inputs in Preferences
+ Added a custom resource import from another project in Library
+ Video Cursor can be styled (Cross or Circle)
+ On Windows, prevent multiple instances of same MadMapper executable

* Optimized engine when working with many outputs

About MadMapper

 

Created and developed by 1024 architecture and GarageCube since 2010, the concept of MadMapper emerged during an early edition of the Mapping Festival in Geneva, when Frz from 1024 and Boris from GarageCube discussed how to properly map a visual content in real time, in real space.

 

MadMapper was therefore born from the encounter between an artistic collective - 1024 - and a software development company - GarageCube -. The essence of the software comes from this deep relationship between artistic needs and technical solutions to make the dream happen.The core idea is to make the technical aspect of a digital installation as easy as possible, in order to focus on the creative matter rather than spend hours on the setup. 

 

MadMapper is an easy-to-use yet powerful tool to map video into the space, control lights and LED bars, and since version 5, to control and use laser beams in the same intuitive way.

 

Led by 1024 in Paris / France and GarageCube in Geneva / Switzerland, the MAD team has grown to include a developer dream-team based in Brussels / Belgium and an international community of MAD users. The software is used worldwide by countless visual and digital artists, scenographers, stage designers, Vjs, and many others creative people to produce smart digital art installation or big shows in Las Vegas!

 

MadMapper is the tool that we dreamed of.

 

Be Mad and enjoy!

 

The MAD team

MadMapper, the Ultimate Mapping Software

 

MadMapper is a leading software for video and light mapping used globally by visual artists, scenographers, and many more. Built for creative freedom and live performance, it allows users to map content onto any surface - flat or complex - in real time.

 

Key features include support for multiple simultaneous inputs/outputs, advanced mapping tools, a built-in library of textures and effects, audio reactivity, real-time video playback, DMX/Art-Net lighting control, sequencing & timeline, export, and laser mapping - enabling users to control laser projectors - with unprecedented accuracy and flexibility.

 

It remains highly accessible to newcomers while offering deep customization for professionals. MadMapper is widely adopted by art schools, institutions, media labs, with training programs around the world, fostering a strong community of learners and creators who shape the future of audiovisual expression.

MadMapper 6 is out. Check it out!

Video Mapping

 

MadMapper is the reference software for real-time video mapping, combining an intuitive interface with professional technical capabilities.

 

It enables video and generative content to be projected onto simple or complex surfaces, thanks to many advanced mapping tools. Users can precisely map various content onto 2D and 3D volumes with total control.

 

The integrated video engine is ultra-high-performance, capable of handling very high resolutions and playing formats such as HAP, ProRes, standard H.264 and more. It supports multiple simultaneous video outputs, making it ideal for immersive installations and large-scale events.

 

MadMapper also supports live sources via Syphon, Spout, NDI or camera feeds, and offers perfectly fluid playback, whether looped, triggered or timeline-driven.

 

The software also includes a full-featured shader editor, enabling the integration of generative effects in real time, and an audio engine that enables content or effects to be driven from sound (spectrum analysis, beat detection, etc.). Compatibility with standard protocols (MIDI, OSC, DMX/Art-Net, Ableton Link) makes it a particularly connected and powerful creative platform.

Light Mapping

 

MadMapper gives you precise creative control over light thanks to its powerful MadLight feature. The software natively supports DMX, Art-Net, or sACN protocols.

 

Its integrated LED scanner facilitates spatial calibration of installations, and coupled with video, audio or shaders, light mapping in MadMapper paves the way for dynamic, immersive and totally synchronized light scenography.

MadMapper Key Features

  • Ultra fast Video Player: Playback at huge resolutions
  • Multiple projectors: Connect as many projectors as your computer can handle
  • Bezier Masking: Hand-cut, trim and mask your content with advanced Bezier geometry
  • Mesh Warping: Precisely fit your content to real surfaces with professional warping tools
  • Spout / Syphon / NDI: Share content with other graphic applications
  • Live controls: Connect any MIDI/OSC controller to MadMapper and perform in realtime
  • Material Editor: Use the MadMapper shader editor to create your generative texture and share them with the community
  • 3D Calibration: Match your 3D model to the real world
  • Space Scanner: Use your camera to capture the projector’s point of view
  • Built-in generative content: Colors, patterns, grids, text, and generative shaders natively included

All MadMapper features are available with any paid license type - perpetual, temporary, or educational.

Only the Demo version includes feature restrictions.

MadLaser

 

MadLaser is an extension of MadMapper dedicated to laser mapping. Compatible with multiple Laser hardware devices, MadLaser transforms any shape, text or generative content into laser trajectories in real time, and above all, in true MadMapper fashion.

 

Create fluid, sharp and expressive animations with ease, directly synchronized with video, audio or lighting. Accessible and powerful, the MadLaser extension opens up a new dimension in audiovisual creation.

MadLaser Key Features

  • Unlimited laser outputs: As many as your computer can handle
  • Multi Hardware supported: Ether Dream, ShowNET, Helios, FB3, FB4 (with Pangolin and Windows), AVB/Dante, LaserCube, IDN
  • Laser Bezier lines: Ultra-precise vector graphics
  • 3D object rendering from .OBJ format
  • Realtime video vectorization: Hardware-accelerated image analysis and processing
  • Ilda files import / export
  • Vector Materials: Real-time shader based
  • Up to 100 kpps scanners: High-definition graphics
  • Laser Soft Edge on laser quads
  • Laser Dispatch: Spread complex content over multiple lasers

MadLaser is an extension of MadMapper and cannot operate as a standalone application.

A MadMapper license is required.

MadProjectorControl

 

The MadProjectorControl extension uses the PJLink protocol to remotely control any number of compatible video projectors.

Fully cueable, this extension allows you to schedule and automate power and shutter activity.

 

Main features:

  • Compatible with any PJLink-compliant device
  • Control any number of projectors
  • Cuable, schedulable and automatable
  • Allows power on/off and shutter remotely
  • Displays device information

Like MadLaser, MadProjectorControl is an extension and requires a MadMapper license.

MadAI

 

With one of our latest addition, MadAI, transform any ideas into dynamic visuals without writing a single line of code.

Material (shader) generation, 2D effects or laser animations: just think of a prompt and MadAI will take care of the rest.

Need inspiration? Mix existing content from the library using AI.

MadAI requires credits to make requests!

MiniMad

 

MiniMad is a hardware plug-and-play device designed to playback your MadMapper setups with automatic network synchronization for multi-projection or DMX/Art-net output to control lighting and LED equipment.

 

MiniMad makes your installation easy and affordable: it hooks up to a projector and plays content on surfaces exported from MadMapper. Alternatively, you can achieve an equivalent outcome through light mapping.

 

Small by size but feature-rich: With the tiny MiniMad, you export quad, triangle circle or mask surfaces as well as their content from a selected projector in MadMapper. You can also switch the MiniMad to lighting mode and output DMX/Artnet channel data to your light fixtures.

 

Discreet and Autonomous: the MiniMad can run on its own for a very long time: we have one unit in the lab running for more than a year! In case of a power failure, the MiniMad will automatically restart without any user intervention. All the mapping modifications you do are automatically saved on the SD card.

 

Team Power: multiple MiniMads can be synchronized with each other over Ethernet to make a cluster of synchronized video players. Zero configuration needed! MadMapper will automatically split movies and optimize files for playback.

 

MiniMad Main Features

  • Automatic synchronisation of video media playback when multiple MiniMads are connected to the same Ethernet network
  • In-depth quality export with precise video controls
  • Up to 64 universes for ArtNet/DMX
  • Autonomous playback of content recorded from MadMapper
  • Multi-channel audio when using Light mode
  • Native video playback up to 1080p30 in optimal conditions.
  • Physical controls with friendly buttons to tweak your mapping directly on location
  • Video or Light: 2 playback modes available
  • VideoWall easy setup - one click full automated process
  • Zero configuration, as simple as that
  • Playback modes: loop, random, list... configure your MiniMad to playback your videos the way you want
  • Mesh Warping and Perspective Pinning with adjustable manual controls.
  • Remote control your MiniMads directly from MadMapper

 

Technical Specifications

  • Raspberry Pi 2
  • 7 buttons control panel
  • 1x HDMI output up to 1080p (1920x1080 at 60Hz)
  • Size: 9 x 6 x 3 cm (approx. 3.5 x 2.3 x 1.2 inches)
  • MiniMad is setup for either video mapping or light mapping; it cannot do both at the same time. Use different units to do so.
  • Media playback (video) is automatically synced when MiniMad units are connected to the same Ethernet network. This can induce a one-frame delay between the different units. Therefore the device is not suitable for blending/soft-edge.
  • For MiniMads that are running continuously for months, ie. for an installation, we recommend using industrial-grade Micro SD cards as well as having backup SD cards with your project already exported.

MadMapper History

2025

MadMapper 6

 

MadMapper 6 is a landmark update introducing the brand-new Timeline feature.

It's an exciting new way to synchronize and run an entire show, in true MadMapper fashion. And for the first time, users can natively export their mapping work as a video file.

DMX tools also receive a major improvement: DMX now samples the output directly, eliminating the need for loopbacks.

Among the many new features, this version also debuts a refreshed user interface for a cleaner, sharper overall experience.

 

Features

  • Timelines
  • Montage tracks, Audio tracks
  • Timelines grid
  • Markers
  • Export
  • DMX sampling
  • Projects workspaces
  • Offline library
  • Optimized UI

MadAI

 

MadAI uses artificial intelligence to help you develop realtime materials, FX and more!

Introduced in MadMapper Version 5.7.0, the new feature allows users to create parametric realtime visuals, laser materials, or 2D effects surfaces.

MadAI can also be used to remix existing content from the Library.

All without knowing how to code.

2023

MadMapper 5.5

 

MadMapper version 5.5 unveils the MAD Laser Scanner, which turns your camera and laser into a 2D spatial scanning tool!

The update also introduces 4 new modules, support of HAP-R codec on Windows, a project-backup system, and more.

 

Features

  • Laser scanner
  • AutoSave & project Backup
  • 4 new Modules for automatically executing a Cue right after opening a project
  • 3D Particles generator
  • HapR Codec support
  • "Adjust movie frame rate" option in the MiniMad video's advanced export settings
  • New import of SVG & Export SVG buttons on masks and lines surfaces
  • Fullscreen button on the main window

2022

MadProjectorControl

 

The new MadProjectorControl extension is introduced with MadMapper version 5.1.0.

It uses the PJLink protocol to remotely control any number of video projectors.

Totally cueable, this extension allows you to schedule and automate power and shutter activity, directly from MadMapper.

2021

MadMapper 5

 

MadMapper 5 is released with a major new feature: MadLaser, an extension module for controlling laser beams through the MadMapper interface, using the integrated generative texture library.

The extension also enables real-time vectorization of video content.

 

Features

  • MadLaser laser control interface
  • Masks, lines, and surfaces can be shaped by laser
  • Multi protocol laser: ILDA, FB4, Lasercube
  • Real-time video vectorization
  • Laser Dispatch: precise combinations of multiple lasers.
  • Real-time laser texture programming
  • GPU particle module

2020

MadMapper 4

 

MadMapper becomes a Live Coding tool!

Version 4.0 implements a range of surface effects as well as a code editor, enabling graphic shaders to be created directly in MadMapper in real-time.

The update features a more comprehensive interface, making the software more accessible and versatile.

Masks can now be created using Bezier lines and curves, and the texture library is now a shared online library, enabling all users to share and download an exponential number of animated textures.

 

Features

  • New texture library
  • New DMX monitor
  • Multiple masks
  • Surface effects & feathering
  • Surface code editor
  • Connection to Arduino sensors

2017

MadMapper 3

 

The new MadMapper updates are huge: first and foremost, the major evolution is the introduction of a generative texture library and an editor for coding them.

But this version also marks MadMapper's entry into Windows compatibility - previously developed for MacOS only - as well as compatibility with Ableton Live software, reinforcing the link between digital art and musical composition.

Finally, the software adopts a new interface based on the Scene model, facilitating navigation between the various parameters of each project.

 

Features

  • Texture library
  • Texture code editor
  • Ableton Link
  • Parametric scene system
  • 3D lighting
  • Live video input
  • Space Scanner: recognizes a 3D volume
  • 3D calibration
  • Video effects
  • Scene settings interface
  • Texture code editor
  • Texture library

2015

MiniMad

 

MiniMad is a standalone player that autonomously runs a MadMapper project previously exported to the device.

This portable tool was designed in response to a need at 1024 Architecture: the ability to activate several installations running MadMapper simultaneously, without having to tie up an expensive computer for each project.

MiniMad was initially targeted at galleries and museums for long-term exhibitions.

2014

MadMapper 2

 

The new features turn the software into a mapping and VJing tool.

MadMapper is now compatible with PS3/PS4 MIDI controllers and joysticks, and it's finally possible to implement 3D objects and surfaces, as well as import SVG lines drawn from other software.

 

Features

  • MIDI protocol
  • 3D objects and surfaces
  • Import of SVG lines
  • LED control in DMX language

2013

MAD Orb

 

An early MadMapper project by 1024 architecture and GarageCube for which an unfolded 2D LED matrix is remapped onto the physical 3D object.

A series of specific lighting behaviors are programmed in MadMapper to activate the light architecture in real-time, following the rhythm of the DJs' mixes.

If you're planning projection mapping, you'll need a projector. Most modern models will work; brightness, throw distance, and lens options simply depend on your project’s scale. We'll cover the key considerations below.

Projectors

Which projector should you choose?

 

The answer depends entirely on your project.  A small indoor installation requires very different equipment than lighting up Berghain's main floor or the Eiffel Tower façade.

Consider factors like projection distance, surface size and material, and the surrounding environment.

Image Resolution

A projector’s resolution determines how many pixels it displays, directly influencing image sharpness and clarity.

Higher resolution means more detailed, precise projection—particularly important for large screens or detailed content.

A minimum of 720p HD is recommended for basic use.

For sharper, more detailed projections, Full HD (1080p) is preferable, and 4K is ideal for the highest level of clarity and precision (think large surfaces or high level of details).

Brightness

Brightness is crucial when selecting a projector. Measured in lumens, it reflects the intensity of the light the device emits. Generally, more lumens produce a clearer image that remains visible even in brightly lit environments.

Contrast

Contrast is the difference between the light and dark areas in a projected image, measured as a ratio. Higher the ratios create greater distinction between light and dark areas. Keep in mind that true black doesn't exist in projection - the darkest areas appear as a very deep gray.

Refresh Rate

The refresh rate, measured in Hertz (Hz), indicates how many times per second the image updates on the screen. Standard refresh rates are 50 Hz or 60 Hz, depending on regional broadcasting standards. Higher refresh rates produce smoother motion and reduce flickering, especially noticeable with fast-moving content.

Ambient Light

Ambient light fundamentally affects projection quality and visibility.

Excessive surrounding light washes out colors, reduces contrast, and makes images appear faded or unclear.

For optimal results, minimize external light sources by darkening the environment or choose projectors with higher brightness to compensate.

Using Multiple Projectors

You may need several projectors simultaneously for your mapping, typically when projecting onto very large surfaces.

First, ensure your computer has the necessary resources, particularly graphics card capabilities. Running multiple projectors simultaneously is very demanding for entry-level computers.

If your computer doesn't have enough outputs, you will need to use an external device to add more, see Output Considerations above.

Preventing Dust

Caution! Projectors tend to accumulate dust, which can cause overheating or malfunctions.
Clean the ventilation system regularly to maintain performance and extend service life.

Transport Safety

Handle projectors carefully when moving or setting them up to maintain performance and extend lifespan. Always transport equipment in protective cases, avoid sudden shocks or vibrations, and allow the projector to cool down completely before packing. Proper handling preserves both optical quality and internal components over time.

Lighting & LED

MadMapper's native MadLight feature for light mapping supports DMX, Art-Net and sACN protocols, allowing control of LED fixtures, moving heads, and other compatible lighting devices.

DMX Protocol

DMX (Digital Multiplex) is the industry-standard protocol for controlling lighting equipment including LED fixtures, dimmers, moving heads, and other stage devices. Originally developed for theater and live events, it's now a cornerstone of interactive and audiovisual installations. DMX sends digital signals for precise parameter control.

Art-Net, sACN Protocol

These network-based protocols transmit DMX data over standard Ethernet.

They make large-scale lighting setups more flexible and manageable, sending multiple DMX universes through a single network cable.

Unlike traditional DMX connections limited by cable length and channel count, they distribute data efficiently across long distances and complex installations.

Broadcast vs Unicast

Broadcast (preferred for small installations): transfer data to all network device simultaneously. Easy to configure.

Unicast (preferred for bigger installations including a lof of DMX universes): transfer data to each network device independently with much better performances, sending data only where needed. Requires extra configuration.

Multicast (sACN) is often preferred for large installations, it reduces the network traffic and ensures a simultaneous signal reception on all devices.

LED by garageCube

Since its successful Kickstarter launch, LED by garageCube has remained user-friendly and highly adaptable, designed for beginners and professionals alike. Each unit assembles easily using sturdy yet lightweight aluminum supports, making it simple to transport, set up, and reconfigure.

 

The system offers an ideal introduction to DMX lighting, while remaining perfectly suited for scalable, upgradeable installations. Expand your setup at any time by adding LED bars in different formats (available in RGB or Pure White) or incorporate DMX bulbs.

 

While LED by garageCube is compatible with any software supporting the DMX protocol, it truly shines with MadMapper. Developed alongside MadMapper’s MadLight feature, the system integrates seamlessly, allowing precise, flexible, and enjoyable light design and control.

While this hardware works seamlessly with MadMapper, you can use any other DMX-compatible equipment that fits your project needs.

USB-DMX Controllers

To enable communication between your computer (and MadMapper) and your DMX hardware, you need a dedicated controller to interpret the transmitted signal. It's mandatory.

 

A USB-to-DMX controller is typically a small plug-and-play box controlling a few universes. For instance, the garageCube controller (no driver required for MadMapper) handles up to 512 DMX channels (8 meters of -any- LED by garageCube).

Since MadMapper 4, multiple usb-to-dmx controllers can be used simultaneously by adding multiple DMX Router Modules.

That being said, we recommend an Art-Net controller for serious installations.

Art-Net Controllers

Art-Net protocol transmits data over Ethernet networks - ideal for large-scale, synchronized lighting projects. Art-Net controllers are much larger and more capable than usb-dmx controllers.

 

They handle multiple universes; for example, the garageCube controller can manage up to 8 DMX universes (64 meters of LED by garageCube).

Note that web-based admin setup is a standard for such controllers.

It's once again the perfect companion for large installations requiring multiple DMX universes management.

Moreover, it's considered the most reliable option as well as the most versatile one since it allows to control other DMX devices at the same time.

ShowNET

MadMapper supports the ShowNET protocol, so any LaserWorld projector with ShowNET works directly with just a network cable (Auto IP works fine). For best performance, put ShowNET devices on a network without other traffic.

 

https://www.laserworld.com

Check your laser device documentation to see how to setup the ShowNET dip switch corresponding to your network mode (DHCP / Auto-IP or static IP).

If your ShowNET device appears as a destination in MadMapper’s Laser Output list but fails to connect (status remains Disconnected), check that you do not have multiple network interfaces using the same IP address range (e.g. 192.168.0.xxx / 255.255.255.0).

If another interface (such as Wi-Fi or a secondary network adapter) is using the same IP range, either disable that interface, assign it a different IP range, or switch the ShowNET pins to Auto-IP mode. In this case, set your computer’s network interface to DHCP as well, so both devices automatically assign themselves Auto-IP addresses (169.254.xxx.xxx / 255.255.0.0).

Recommend Laser Devices for Testing

It depends on the budget and intended projects.

For graphics: needs accurate scanning, precise and small beam, low divergence and good diodes alignment.

For video projection with laser overlay: a small beam (low divergence) works better.

For architectural mapping, atmospheric effects, clubbing or festivals: prioritize power over sharpness.

For museum installations: choose a low power with sharp beam.

An example: the LaserWorld Tarm 3W offers good whites (no need to reduce blue by 50%), adequate sharpness and 3W sufficient for atmospheric effects.

Many laser devices are comparable in quality. LaserWorld is notable for having an integrated Ethernet DAC (ShowNET), eliminating the need for an external DAC (Ethernet or USB to ILDA).

Safety Recommendations

Lasers are powerful and dangerous, handle them carefully with audience safety in mind.

Comply with local regulations.

MadMapper cannot be held responsible for misuse of laser equipment.

Above all, never project laser beams toward the audience. Always use a hardware safety switch and define a dedicated safety zone.

Also, protect your laser hardware by ensuring the scan rate remains within safe limits.

Licensing Options

Seats = Computers

In the MadMapper licensing system, computers are referred to as seats. One seat = one computer, whether Mac or PC.

The number of seats included in a license determines how many devices can run MadMapper simultaneously. For example, a 2-seat license allows you to use MadMapper on two computers at the same time.

You will have to log out from one of your 2 computers before being able to use MadMapper on a third one.

Temporary vs Perpetual

Temporary Licenses

Temporary licenses let you select both the number of seats and the duration of the license activation.

You can start with a minimum of 1 seat for 1 month.

Temporary licenses never renew automatically.

They expire at the end of the selected term, you'll have to grab a new one to continue to use MadMapper.

Perpetual Licenses

Perpetual licenses are lifetime licenses that do not expire. They are designed for long-term use and start with a minimum of 2 seats, up to 20.

You can store an unlimited number of licenses in your MadMapper account, whether they are temporary or perpetual, making it easy to manage multiple projects or teams from a single account.

EDUCATION Licenses

EDUCATION licenses are available in both temporary and perpetual versions and are identical in every way to their standard license equivalents.

These licenses are offered at a discount to support students, teachers, and schools in learning MadMapper.

To apply for the EDUCATION offer, please visit this page: https://madmapper.com/education

Generators

 

The generators are built-in and are initially intended for testing and calibration.

They are rendered at a specified pixel size in a texture.

Note that generators also include the Text Generator as well Materials if you drag and drop one in the Generators list.

Materials

 

Materials are generative shaders, rendered directly on the output destination (projector or preview windows).

Unlike generators where only one rendering will be done regardless of their number in your surfaces, the materials are rendered separately on each of the surfaces where they are used.

The materials are allowing extra precision at high resolution, at the expense of rendering speed.

Materials can be dragged to the Generators category in order to convert them to a rendered texture at the same specified rendering dimensions.

Timeline Scheduler

 

Timeline Scheduler ensure a timeline get started when we’re inside the time range, between Start time (hour/minute/seconds) & End time, if the “Date” settings matches current day.

 

In Depth:

 

The timeline (a scene or a cue, animated or not) will be started when:

  • Loading the project and we’re inside the time range.
  • When entering the time range (because time elapses or because we’re editing Start/End time).

The timeline will be stopped when:

  • Leaving the time range (because time elapses or because we’re editing Start/End time) while the timeline was started by this same module.

If "End/Stop on Loop End” is enabled, the timeline will be paused when reaching loop end (except if playhead is after loop end).

 

If the target bank is not the current bank, the scheduler will not change current bank but it will start the timeline in the desired bank.

When timeline is started, if grid has horizontal or grid exclusivity, it will be handled, like if user clicked the play button.

So End time doesn’t change anything for a non animated scene or cue, except when loading project (so on computer startup in an fixed installation with project loading at computer start).

MadMapper FAQ 

Is MadMapper available for Windows?

MadMapper 6 is available for PC and requires at least Windows 10.

Please note that a 64-bit Windows system is required to run MadMapper and that the software is not meant to run in a virtual machine.

 

Is MadMapper available for Mac?

MadMapper 6 is available on Mac computers and requires at least macOS 10.13 High Sierra.

Please note that MadMapper 6 is not meant to run in a virtual machine.

For older system versions, a MadMapper build compatible with macOS 10.9 - 10.12 is available in the Download section of your user account.

This version is not as thoroughly tested as the official one and may feature lower performance and limitations compared to official builds.

Is MadMapper ready for Apple M computers?

Since v5, MadMapper is an M native application, fully compatible with macOS Big Sur, Monterey.

These builds, as well as Intel ones, are available in the Download section of your user account.

Is there a difference between the Mac and the Windows version?

The two versions are identical with the exact same features.

Differences in software performance won’t be the result of your OS but of your computer’s resources.

Is it possible to purchase a single seat license?

Only rental licenses can be purchased for 1 computer.

Perpetual licenses start with 2 seats: we’ve added a spare seat in case of computer failure during a performance or show.

Can I extend my license with additional seats?

It’s not possible to add seats to your existing license.

Can I share my multiple seats license with someone else?

Sharing a license is prohibited in the software user agreement.

What are the minimum hardware requirements to run MadMapper 6?

You will need a computer with at least 300 MB of disk space and at least 2 GB of RAM and any GPU compatible with OpenGL 3.3.

For more advanced use, you’ll also need at least a 2-4 cores CPU, and 8 GB of RAM. An SSD drive and a dedicated GPU are highly recommended as well.

What would be an optimal hardware configuration for MadMapper 6?

In order to take full advantage of the advanced features of MadMapper such as heavy use of materials, here’s an example of recommended configuration for Windows : 6-8 cores CPU, Nvidia 1080 up to 20xx GPU.

For the Mac version, we recommend iMac, Mac Pro and MacBook Pros over standard MacBooks. Avoid Intel integrated GPUs and mechanical drives.

Do you have an educational offer?

We do have educational pricing that applies to students, teachers, instructors and schools requiring MadMapper as part of their instruction, training or for research purposes.

To apply for an educational discount please contact our Support.

Can you apply for the Educational offer as an association / non-profit organization?

The Educational offer is restricted to students, teachers and schools. Please refer to the dedicated section.

What is the difference between the educational and standard versions?

There are no limitations for the educational version of MadMapper, both versions are identical, although you are not allowed to use it for commercial purposes.

What is the difference between the full and rental versions?

The rental license is time limited while the full version is perpetual.

Otherwise they are identical.

What is the difference between the full and the demo versions?

The demo version is a free version, its purpose is to try the software in order to figure out if it fits your project needs.

It is not a version aimed to professional work and it comes with several limitations: a watermark is shown on input, output and output preview, loading/saving a project is disabled, export to SVG/PNG/PDF is disabled, spacial Scanner is limited and cropped to 1/4th of its resolution, DMX lighting devices will blackout once every 30 seconds, material installation and publishing from the library is disabled.

Please note that it is not possible to authorize the demo version.

Once you’ve purchased the Full version, you must download the most recent version of MadMapper in the Download section of your user account.

How can I update or upgrade my license?

Updates are available in the Downloads section of your user account. You can also upgrade each of your license directly from your user account.

In which language(s) is MadMapper available?

The software is only available in English.

How do I get the MadMapper License Agreement?

It’s available within the MadMapper Menu, under Preferences.

I am supposed to be exempt from VAT, how do I proceed?

If you have a valid EU VAT number, you can enter it in your user account or at checkout.

VAT will then be excluded from the total amount of your order.

Do you deliver your products / items anywhere in the world?

Yes, our software, as well as our hardware products such as the MiniMad or the LED by garageCube can be purchased on our site from any country, with the exception of Russia, Iran and North Korea.

About MadMapper

 

Created and developed by 1024 architecture and GarageCube since 2010, the concept of MadMapper emerged during an early edition of the mapping festival in Geneva, when Frz from 1024 and Boris from GarageCube discussed about how to properly map a visual content in realtime, in real space.

MadMapper was therefore born from the encounter between an artistic label - 1024 - and a software development company - GarageCube -. The essence of the software is coming from this deep relationship between artistic needs and technical solutions to make the dream happen.

The core idea is to make the technical aspect of a digital installation as easy as possible, in order to focus on the creative matter rather than to spend hours on the setup.

MadMapper is an easy to use yet powerful tool to map video into the space, control lights and led bars, and, since version 5, to control and use laser beams in the same funny way and process.

Headed by 1024 in Paris / France and GarageCube in Geneva / Switzerland, the mad team grows up with a developper dream-team based in Brussels / Belgium and an international community of mad users.

The software is used worldwide by countless visual and digital artist, scenographers, stage designers, Vjs, and many others creative people to produce smart digital art installation or big shows in Las Vegas !

MadMapper is the tool that we dreamed of.

Be mad and enjoy !

MadMapper, the ultimate mapping software

 

MadMapper is a leading software for video and light mapping used globally by visual artists, scenographers, and so on. Built for creative freedom and live performance, it allows users to map content onto any surface - flat or complex - in real time.

Key features include support for multiple outputs, advanced mesh warping, real-time video playback, audio reactivity, DMX/Art-net lighting control, and recently laser mapping, enabling users to control laser projectors with unprecedented accuracy and flexibility.

It remains highly accessible to newcomers, while offering deep customization for professionals. Therefore MadMapper is widely adopted by art schools, media labs, and training programs around the world, fostering a strong community of learners and creators who shape the future of audiovisual expression.

Video Mapping

 

MadMapper is the reference software for real-time video mapping, combining an intuitive interface with professional technical capabilities.

It enables video and generative content to be projected onto simple or complex surfaces, thanks to advanced warping, Bézier masking or multi-surface management tools. Users can precisely map video onto 2D and 3D volumes, with total control over distortion and content synchronization.

The integrated video engine is ultra-high-performance, capable of handling very high resolutions and playing formats such as HAP, ProRes, standard H264 and more. It supports multiple simultaneous video outputs, making it ideal for immersive installations and large-scale events.

MadMapper also supports live sources via Syphon, Spout, NDI or camera feeds, and offers perfectly fluid playback, whether looped, triggered or timeline-driven.

The software also includes a full-featured GLSL shader editor, enabling the integration of generative effects in real time, and an audio engine that enables video or effects to be driven from sound (spectrum analysis, beat detection, etc.). Compatibility with standard protocols (MIDI, OSC, DMX/Artnet, Ableton Link) makes it a particularly connected and powerful creative platform.

Light Mapping

 

MadMapper gives you precise, creative control over light, thanks to its powerful MadLight feature. The software indeed natively supports DMX, Art-Net, or sACN protocols.

Its integrated LED scanner facilitates spatial calibration of installations, and coupled with video, audio or shaders, light mapping in MadMapper paves the way for dynamic, immersive and totally synchronized light scenography.

MiniMad

 

MiniMad is an hardware plug-and-play device designed to playback your MadMapper setups with automatic network synchronization for multi-projection or DMX / Artnet output to control lighting and LED equipment.

 

MiniMad makes your installation easy and affordable: it hooks up to a projector and plays movie files on surfaces exported from MadMapper. Put your expensive and bulky computers out of a job.

Your MadMapper license can be used on one to several computers (seats).

You can switch your license from a computer to another at any time and as many time as you want. You'll only have to logout first from the previous computer(s).

If you don't have access to one of your computer anymore you can remotely log it out from your license by using a reset.

Such procedure is directly available in your MadMapper user account, license tab.

Please beware that it's an emergency procedure, therefore limited in time for security reasons.

I can’t import my license

If you no longer have access to one of your computer(s) for the reasons mentioned above or for other reasons, you will not be able to de-authorize it from the software.

Tips and Tricks

Ableton Sync

 

We made a demo video available here (only for beat matching) : https://youtu.be/0MbcimSV2VY

Adjust perspective for surfaces groups

If you select a surface group, the geometric adjustment in the output will only change X and Y value.

In MadMapper 4/5 you can activate “perspective” option in the group settings. In previous releases, press “alt” when moving the handle of the group, it will do perspective.

With a multi-selection of surfaces ("shadow group") press "alt" when moving the handle of the group, it will do perspective as well.

Assigning multiple OSC channel per control

It's actually limited to one assignment to a control per controller type (MIDI/OSC/DMX/etc.).

However there are two options: create cues with various "visibility" setups (add the visibility of your surfaces in some cues using Cues "Edit" mode, check Scenes & Cues doc in Help menu or look at youtube video tutorials) or use the "Controls Combiner" module to combine multiple inputs to a single control.

Background image not displayed in the output window

The output remains black if no content is loading.

The background image is only for preview.

Broadcast vs Unicast for Light mapping

Broadcast (preferred for small installations) is transferring data to all network device simultaneously and is easy to configure.

Unicast (preferred for bigger installations including a lof of DMX universes) is transferring data to each network device independently and have much better performances by sending data only where is needed.

Unicast need an extra configuration.

Cameras for live video input

MadMapper supports cameras as a source input.

On macOS you can use any USB camera for live feeds as long as it is supported by QuickTime.

We can’t recommend any specific one as we have not tested all cameras on the market.

On Windows, you can use any camera that supports DirectShow (most of them do, but check first).

Cameras for Spatial Scanning

For the spacial scanner feature we only support the Canon SDK, meaning you can use a Canon camera in full resolution, otherwise other cameras can work as webcams if compatible with quicktime (macOS) or directshow (windows).

You may not get the proper full resolution of your camera as the video signal will be processed through usb, through webcam.

 

macOS: everything that can be seen via QuickTime (since both QuickTime and MadMapper use AVFoundation for the cameras), and if the manufacturer provides an AVFoundation driver or uses a standard protocol.

 

Windows: the manufacturer must provide DirectShow support. We strongly recommend that you try the MadMapper Demo to make sure your hardware is compatible before purchasing the software. Other recommendations: the less compression the better. The higher the resolution the better. A second-hand Canon camera (entry-level) is a good way to go.

Can I scale multiple selected 3D surfaces at once?

3D Surfaces are mostly made for calibrating to the physical world object - calibrated objects can't be moved afterwards.

This is the reason why 3D surfaces cannot be modified by "group" selection.

H264 is the standard recommend video codec.

You must use two surfaces to do that. Fading normally smoothly change the parameter, but we can't fade the "FX Name" parameter, so it just switches.

Recommend lens for spatial scanning

The best is to have at least one pixel of the camera for one pixel of the video projector. More is better. So if you can have a lens that makes your projection area fill the camera picture it's enough.

Scenes and Cues in a nutshell

In MadMapper you can create scenes & cues (basically presets) in the same grid. Scenes is the first row. Scenes are restoring the complete state of your mapping (surfaces, fixtures, medias, and some modules). Cues are storing a user chosen set of parameters (ie you can store only surfaces colors on a cue grid row, while storing different sets of media assignment on another row).

Short throw projectors and 3D objects

Short throw projectors are not supported for 3D calibration simply because it's impossible.

A short-throw projector will show a flat-uniform picture at a certain distance on a flat surface parallel to the projector but the picture is quite altered in the space.

However by using quad mesh warping with bezier, you might be able to project your content but not using a 3D object.

What You Need to Run MadMapper

MadMapper is designed to be lightweight, flexible, and compatible with a wide range of hardware configurations.

Whether you’re working on a small projection mapping project or a large-scale installation, here’s what you need to know about supported systems and recommended setups.

 

At its core, all you need to get started with MadMapper is a computer running macOS or Windows

Also meaning even with the Demo version you can explore the interface, design your mappings, and experiment with ideas entirely on-screen.

 

The minimum hardware requirements to run MadMapper is a computer running macOS or Windows

At least 300 MB of disk space and a minimum of 2 GB of RAM and a GPU compatible with OpenGL 3.3.

 

We recommend a CPU with at least 2–4 cores and a minimum of 8 GB of RAM. An SSD and a dedicated GPU are also highly recommended for optimal performance.

 

MadMapper 6 runs seamlessly on both macOS and Windows, offering the same powerful performances and features across platforms.

macOS: version 11 or higher

Windows: version 10 or higher

 

There is no “better” platform, both systems are fully supported and deliver excellent performance.

 

Your choice will mostly come down to personal preference, budget, and the kind of projects you plan to create. Some artists prefer macOS for its streamlined workflow and system stability, while others choose Windows for its flexibility and broader hardware options.

 

Ultimately, both platforms let you get the most out of MadMapper’s creative potential.

 

macOS Recommendations

MadMapper performs well even on modest Apple hardware, making it an excellent choice for portability and reliability.

  • Entry-level MacBooks (such as MacBook Air or older MacBook Pro models) are perfectly fine for common projection mapping tasks.

  • If you plan to work extensively with heavy shaders, multiple video inputs, large 3D content, etc. you’ll benefit from a more powerful GPU (graphics card).

  • Even a second-hand MacBook can be suitable for light to medium use.

MadMapper has been a native M-software for Apple Silicon (M-series) computers since version 5.

Windows Recommendations

MadMapper runs equally well on Windows systems, as long as they’re properly configured.

  • Processor (CPU): Choose a recent, high-performance model (Intel i5/i7/i9 or AMD Ryzen series for instance). Avoid entry-level CPUs, which can bottleneck performance.
  • Graphics Card (GPU): A dedicated GPU is essential. NVIDIA and AMD cards are both supported.
  • Memory (RAM): At least 8 GB is required; 16 GB or more is recommended for smooth performance.
  • Storage: An SSD drive is strongly recommended for faster project loading and video playback.

Even compact PCs such as Intel NUCs or mini PCs can handle projection mapping surprisingly well, it can be ideal for small or portable setups.

DMX Fixtures - Import / Export from SVG

MadMapper 6.1 comes with Bézier Fixtures which allows new possibilities for importing fixtures from SVG. While MadMapper 5 was only import "line" elements from SVG, MadMapper 6.1 can load "line","rect","circle","ellipse","polygon","polyline","path".

 

Also in MadMapper 6.1 a fixture definition can be set to LED Strip mode or LED Matrix mode. In this case, you can specify the strip length (or matrix size) for each fixture. So if you have a strip with 160 pixels, one with 165, one with 100 pixels, they can all use the Fixture Definition « LED Strip RGB » and you specify the size for each Fixture. Same for matrices.

 

We've also added options to specify fixtures parameters directly your your vector file editor (ie Illustrator, Inkscape etc.). For instance DMX patching (universe / channel) can be specified from the layer "id" exported in SVG file. It is also possible to generate an SVG from a script or with an AI and add DMX patching info as XML tags of the geometry elements in the SVG.

Another improvement : when imported from SVG, layer groups in the SVG will generate fixture groups in MadMapper, it will respect and reproduce the hierarchy.

 

Exporting fixtures to SVG and importing it in a new project will recreate the original setup (fixture types, geometry, line/circle thickness, DMX patching (universe / channel), group hierarchy etc. This make new workflows easy:

  • Create fixture setup in MadMapper, export as SVG and use it in a software like After Effects to create a video animation easiely that will perfectly match fixtures.
  • Create fixture setup in an SVG file from a vector editor (Illustrator) or with an AI and import it, it can also be used in a video editing software to create content.

This document describes how an SVG file will be interpreted by MadMapper when using File / Import Fixtures and choosing an SVG file (CSV import has not been modified).

Additional settings extracted from "id"

The id of a layer can include all necessary parameters to create the fixtures. If the layer id is « MySuperLedStrip », it will just create a fixture with name «  MySuperLedStrip » (fixture type will be deduced from svg geometry type : line, rect etc.).

 

But the id can include extra info. For instance if the id is « MySuperLedStrip__UN__10__CH__12 », the fixture name will be « MySuperLedStrip » and MadMapper will set UNiverse to 10 and CNannel to 12.

Supported data

- « __UN__ » : Universe number (0-32767)

- « __CH__ » : Channel number (1-512)

- « __FT__ » : Fixture Type to create. Possible values : « fixture_bezier », « fixture_line », « fixture_circle », « fixture_quad »

- « __FD__ » : Fixture Definition, for instance « Generic – Pixel RGB » or « GarageCube - SFX-01 W 1m » (Group[space]-[space]Name)

- « __SL__ » : Strip Length (for fixture definition set to LED Strip mode)

- « __MW__ » and « __MH__ » : Matrix Width / Height (for fixture definition set to Matrix mode)

- « __TH__ » : Thickness in pixels of the line & bezier, or thickness pourcentage for circle fixture

Additional settings in XML elements

This data can also be added as attributes of the geometry XML element if editing from a text editor / script or with an AI, it avoid having very long and cryptic Ids:

- « universe » : Universe number (0-32767)

- « channel » : Channel number (1-512)

- « fixture_type » : Fixture Type to create. Possible values : « fixture_bezier », « fixture_line », « fixture_circle », « fixture_quad »

- « fixture_definition » : Fixture Definition, for instance « Generic – Pixel RGB » or « GarageCube - SFX-01 W 1m » (Group[space]-[space]Name)

- « strip_length » : Strip Length (for fixture definition set to LED Strip mode)

- « matrix_width » and « matrix_height » : Matrix Width / Height (for fixture definition set to Matrix mode)

- « thickness » : Thickness in pixels of the line & bezier, or thickness pourcentage for circle fixture

What fixture type will be created

- If « fixture_type » (« __FT__ ») is specified, MadMapper will create a fixture of the chosen type (refer to previous section)

- If the SVG geometry element is a « line » MadMapper will create an « Fixture Line » surface

- If the SVG geometry element is a « rect » and is not rounded (with rx & ry), MadMapper will create an « Fixture Quad » surface

- For any other type it will create a « Fixture Bezier »
